Facts: Heir claimed partial nullity of usufruct legacy, arguing property was partly his under community property regime; failed to challenge father’s prior will leaving everything to mother.
Legal Framework: Legal community property regime; testamentary succession; action for reduction; burden of proof in succession matters.
Interpretative Issues: Whether heir claiming ownership interest in property bequeathed by deceased must challenge all prior wills affecting ownership; who bears burden of proving testator validly disposed of owned property versus property owned pro rata with others.
Legal Principles: Heir claiming property belonged partly to him must prove ownership interest by challenging all relevant prior testamentary dispositions. Failure to bring reduction action against father’s will leaving entire estate to mother means mother validly acquired full ownership, enabling her to dispose of entire property by will. Mere fact that succession declaration was filed only by one party or that will publication occurred after declaration filing does not affect validity of testamentary disposition. Circumstance that attorney who usually represented deceased requested will publication supports validity of testamentary intent.
